title: Isolation of fungal strains from soybean pastes and preparation of DPP‐IV inhibitory peptides from quinoa proteins by fungal fermentation
content:
Abstract

BACKGROUND

The rising global burden of type 2 diabetes mellitus and the side effects of synthetic DPP-IV inhibitors have increased demand for food-derived dipeptidyl peptidase-IV (DPP-IV) inhibitory peptides. Quinoa is a promising source of such bioactive peptides, while fungi from soybean paste exhibit high proteolytic activity. However, the use of fungi to produce quinoa-derived DPP-IV inhibitory peptides via fermentation remains unexplored. This study focused on isolating fungal strains from soybean pastes and preparing DPP-IV inhibitory peptides from quinoa proteins.

RESULTS

Results suggested that 33 strains were isolated from 37 soybean paste samples, among which 16 strains exhibited high protease activity (>30 U mL−1). Among these, three strains, identified as Zygosaccharomyces sp. (a1), Cladosporium sp. (D1), and Talaromyces sp. (E2), yielded fermentates with the most potent DPP-IV inhibitory activities, with median inhibitory concentration (IC50) values of 4.55 ± 0.10, 4.36 ± 0.04, and 4.16 ± 0.04 mg mL−1, respectively. The fermentation conditions of the three strains were optimized using single-factor tests and orthogonal tests. After desalting and simulated gastrointestinal digestion, the product of strain a1 showed significantly enhanced DPP-IV inhibitory activity, with marked inhibition in murine ileal tissue and Caco-2 cells. Furthermore, the peptide VPQNFA was identified as the most potent DPP-IV inhibitor (IC50 = 190.84 ± 8.58 μmol L−1), acting as a competitive inhibitor and forming a stable VPQNFA–DPP-IV complex via multiple hydrogen bonds.

CONCLUSION

These findings provide a novel strategy for preparing DPP-IV inhibitory peptides via fungal fermentation, which holds potential as diabetes-targeted functional food ingredients. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.
